title: Aber derived metrics
description: A list of derived metrics. A derived metric is a value Aber computes from other metrics, such as parts per hour. This file describes exactly what Aber accepts. Anything else is refused, not ignored. The database is the authority: it also checks each input against the catalogue, works out the unit, and refuses a name that is already used for something else.

derivedMetric.title: Derived metric
derivedMetric.description: One derived metric. Its definition is fixed once it is saved. An upload adds a derived metric that does not exist and refuses a name that exists with another definition. It changes the description of one that exists, and never deletes one.

name.description: The derived metric's name, such as Controller/PARTS_PER_HOUR: letters, digits and underscores, with a slash between the parts. A device must not publish it, and it cannot change once saved.

description.description: What the value means, in your words, up to 4,000 characters. Optional. For a metric that exists, an upload sets this description: leave it out and the description is cleared.
examples: Parts made per hour, from the controller's part counter.

kind.description: How the value is computed. `counter_rate` is how fast a counter grows, per hour. `time_in_state` is the share of time a state metric spends in the states listed, from 0 to 1. `sum` adds and subtracts two or more numeric metrics that share one unit.

input.description: The catalogue metric the value is computed from. For `counter_rate`, a numeric counter that counts up and resets to a lower value. For `time_in_state`, a string or boolean metric. It must be in the catalogue and measured, not derived. Not for `sum`.
input.x-derived-says: A derived metric. A derived metric cannot be built on another.

states.description: For `time_in_state`: the values of the input that count as being in the state, at least one, each once. A boolean input reports "true" or "false": write them in quotes. Where the input lists its permitted values, each must be one of them.

inputs.description: For `sum`: the numeric metrics it adds and takes away, two to eight, each once, in the unit they share. Not for the other kinds.

input.title: Input
input.description: One input of a sum: a catalogue metric and whether it is added or taken away.

metric.description: The catalogue name of the input, such as Power/PHASE_A. It must be in the catalogue, numeric and measured, not derived, and in the same unit as the other inputs.
metric.x-derived-says: A derived metric. A derived metric cannot be built on another.

sign.description: 1 to add the input to the total, -1 to take it away.
